newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron talks snagged, U.S. wants Israel-PLO summit.
newsitem.headline: Hebron talks snagged, U.S. wants Israel-PLO summit.

text.p: Israeli-PLO talks on a long-overdue extension of Palestinian self-rule to the West Bank town of Hebron were snagged on four issues on Tuesday, PLO officials said.
The United States, mediating in the negotiations, was awaiting Palestinian agreement to hold a summit meeting with Israel to remove the obstacles, a U.S. official said.
But Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said the problems had to be resolved first to ensure a successful summit between the Palestinians' Yasser Arafat and Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu.
Palestinian officials said Israel was seeking extra powers while Israel's defence minister said it had shown "maximum flexibility".

Hebron, a West Bank flashpoint of violence, is home to 400 militant Jewish settlers and 100,000 Arabs. It was to be handed over to the Palestinians last March but violence, security concerns and Israel's change of government in June delayed the pullback.

It is the last of seven Palestinian centres due to be turned over to Palestinian self-rule under a 1995 peace accord signed by the previous Israeli government. Further rural areas of the occupied West Bank were scheduled to be come under Palestinian control this year but Palestinians have agreed to accept a delay in full implementation until 1998.
Senior Palestinian officials said the sides could quickly overcome remaining obstacles on a Hebron agreement but it was unclear when peace talks would resume.
"The remaining issues are very silly. They could be overcome very quickly," Arafat's adviser Nabil Abu Rdainah told Reuters.
Asked if negotiations had hit yet another snag, Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak said: "I won't enter into details."
But Erekat told Reuters: "We have four problems that need to be resolved before we can conclude the drafting which we hope will be done today."
PLO officials charged the talks were stuck on:
- Israel's demand the Palestinian Authority extradite to Israel Arabs wanted by the Jewish state.
- Israel's demand for a veto over the names of all PLO police set to serve in Hebron.
- Israel's insistence the PLO promise to crack down on militant groups.
- A dispute over Palestinian control of Hebron's al-Ibrahimi mosque, part of a shrine holy to Moslems and Jews as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.
Israeli and Palestine Liberation Organisation peace teams ended a round of late-night talks early on Tuesday after a bomb scare forced them to change venue.

"We have reached our point of maximum flexibility," Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai told reporters on Tuesday. "The Palestinians need to come and sign the agreement and move the process forward."

Progress in the U.S.-brokered talks after months of impasse came during a lightning mediation mission by Jordan's King Hussein on Sunday. The king nudged the sides toward a compromise timetable for three further Israeli withdrawals from rural West Bank areas.
